tasks.short: Evaluate the weight and reliability of case documents

steps.what: Evaluate information in documents against contested issues and competing explanations

tasks.design: Keep the assessment of case documents with the mediator using {DOCS}. Credibility, relevance and conflicting evidence require contextual reasoning; automatic summaries would still require reading the underlying material.
tasks.previous_blocker: A document's apparent clarity does not settle its evidential weight.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change removes the mediator's assessment time.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing an omission from an unreliable account.
tasks.human_edge: Test competing explanations without prejudging the parties.
tasks.altitude: The mediator retains the same assessment responsibility.

reach.learn: Separate established facts from contested assertions

evidence.claim: Document evaluation in contested cases remains a contextual judgement; no local time saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary begins with available case documents and ends with an internal evidence assessment; document gathering and hearing preparation are allocated separately.
No new structured input or automated decision is required. Existing document navigation earns no new labour saving.
Native document search can remain available without changing this judgement step.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, rule or workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Document quality and typical dispute complexity
research_questions: Does an assisted summary reduce total assessment time once source rereading is included?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, incremental=0, net=0. Contested document assessment remains fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define research questions and jurisdiction from the hearing issues
Research laws and precedent decisions and assemble source passages

loop.purpose: Find potentially relevant authorities with quoted source passages
loop.input: Research brief and access-controlled legal corpus
loop.output: Authority shortlist with resolvable citations and applicability caveats
loop.check: Mediator opens authorities and checks holdings, date, jurisdiction and contrary treatment against the issue
loop.stop: After two failed grounded searches or unresolved citations, mediator completes ordinary legal research
loop.why_not_simpler: Native filters retrieve sources but cannot reliably relate varied factual questions to legal reasoning

steps.what: Interpret authorities and prepare the hearing research note

tasks.design: Test native filters in the licensed legal research {OTHER} first. A bounded answer desk drafts a source shortlist from the mediator's brief in {DOCS}; the mediator verifies citations and makes the legal interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searching and connecting relevant authorities requires repeated queries.
tasks.enabler_now: Grounded legal research products can retrieve and draft over named source collections.
tasks.still_hard: Contrary precedent, changed rules and factual distinctions.
tasks.human_edge: Determine what an authority actually means for this hearing.
tasks.altitude: Some retrieval time returns to testing competing legal interpretations.

evidence.claim: Libra supports legal research, drafting and review over Dutch legal sources; this does not establish mediation labour savings.
The digest reports substantial legal research tool error rates, supporting source checking rather than unchecked reliance.
The proposed retrieval-time reduction is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers legal hearing research, excluding evaluation of case documents and the hearing itself.

Mediator produces issue text, jurisdiction, relevant dates, requested authority types and source-access scope in s1; its 20 hours includes capture. The licensed source provider supplies dated authorities and identifiers before s2. Missing metadata triggers manual database research within s2 remaining time.
OTHER means the licensed legal research service. Native search and saved filters are tested before a model workflow; existing search runtime earns no saving.
No generated advice is issued externally. Deployment requires a separate assessment of applicable ADR and data rules.
research_questions: Does verified retrieval halve s2 effort on a representative set of hearing issues?

already_counted.description: Source opening, relevance checking and manual retrieval exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain access scope, evaluate retrieval failures and refresh source tests

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+20+40=80; gross=20, upkeep=4, net=16. Range 0-10 allows difficult issues and extensive source verification.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare subpoenas and administer hearing oaths

steps.what: Determine subpoena requirements and capture recipient and hearing particulars
Prepare subpoenas using the prescribed document form
Verify and issue subpoenas or administer oaths under applicable procedure

tasks.design: Configure a prescribed template in {DOCS} to fill the particulars captured by the arbitrator. The arbitrator checks the rendered version and legal authority before issuing it; oath administration stays personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated form preparation uses time without changing the underlying authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and locked templates can reproduce an approved form.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this arbitrator has the relevant power and which procedure applies.
tasks.human_edge: Exercise procedural authority fairly and confirm participant understanding.
tasks.altitude: The arbitrator spends less time formatting formal documents.

evidence.claim: Native document fields can fill a prescribed form; legal validity and savings require local testing.

assumptions: Boundary covers only this task's subpoena or oath preparation, not general hearing administration. Subpoena and oath branches are a scenario mix, not mandatory actions in every case.

Arbitrator captures case identifier, issuing authority, recipient legal name and service address, hearing date and place, requested attendance or documents, deadline and applicable form version in s1's 20 hours. Missing particulars return to manual completion; no unverified address is used.
Native template fields are tested before custom code. s3 includes rendered-document checking and any manual correction; s2 remains draft-only.
Scenario assumes a meaningful form-preparation share; oath-only cases have zero formatting benefit.
unknowns: Actual subpoena powers and procedural forms
research_questions: Does template preparation reduce total effort while preserving exact required wording?

already_counted.description: Authority verification, document correction, issue approval and oath administration

incremental.description: Maintain prescribed forms and regression-check changed fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact rendered subpoena version with recipient, service address, case, authority, required acts and dates, or exact oath procedure and participant; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+0+50=70, gross=30, upkeep=6, net=24. Range 0-12 allows oath-heavy work and atypical forms requiring manual completion.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange mediation appointments with all parties

steps.what: Collect party availability and capture mediation appointment constraints
Compare availability and prepare feasible mediation appointments
Confirm appointments with parties and send the agreed invitation

tasks.design: Use native availability comparison in {CALENDAR} after the mediator captures the parties' constraints. The mediator resolves conflicts and checks recipients, confidentiality and the agreed slot before sending the invitation through {EMAIL} or {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability sits in separate replies and calendars.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling rules can compare captured windows without interpreting the dispute.
tasks.still_hard: Reluctance to attend, accessibility needs and sensitive recipient lists.
tasks.human_edge: Gain agreement without making scheduling feel coercive.
tasks.altitude: Less calendar comparison; the mediator still owns party agreement.

evidence.claim: Native calendar comparison can suggest slots from explicit availability constraints; this saving is a modelled scenario.

assumptions: Boundary starts with collecting scheduling replies and ends with an agreed invitation; mediation delivery is excluded.

Parties produce availability replies before s1. Mediator captures party identifier, verified contact, allowed visibility, time zone, available windows, duration, location or remote mode and accessibility constraints in s1's 30 hours. Missing or ambiguous fields are resolved by ordinary correspondence in s1 and s3.
Native calendar configuration is tested first. No external invitation is automatically sent and no party sees another party's calendar.
Any additional burden of structured responses is counted as customer incremental work; it is not treated as focal-role saving.
unknowns: Frequency of scheduling changes and confidentiality restrictions
research_questions: Does availability comparison remove enough manual comparison time after constraint capture and rescheduling?

already_counted.description: Party confirmation, conflict handling and final invitation approval

incremental.description: Maintain scheduling rules and check recurring visibility errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact invitation snapshot including parties, recipient visibility, date, time zone, duration, location and agreed accessibility arrangements; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+0+40=70; gross=30, focal upkeep=5, net=25. Range 0-15 assumes repeated availability changes and cautious recipient checks; party labour is outside the focal denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mediator retains evidence assessment and procedural authority while reducing selected retrieval and formatting work.
reach: Coordinate confidential and accessible hearing logistics
role.ambitious_version: A mediator who gives contested evidence and party agreement the time returned by verified preparation tools.
